Subject: Order Form — escrow sequencing, invoicing entity & tax routing clarifications

Hi Jane / BlueHaven team,

Attached is our redline of the Order Form (BlueHaven_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx) with comments focused on three items that came up during legal/procurement review:

- Net terms / invoicing cadence: You asked for Net 45. Our standard for enterprise Order Forms is Net 60 (billing/collections cadence + finance policy). If BlueHaven needs Net 45 for this engagement, we’ll need approval from Revenue Ops and Legal; net effect is a ~0.8% change to pricing cadence (see Ben’s note below).

- Escrow / withholding sequencing for disputed charges: The contract currently references an escrow mechanism for withheld amounts. We propose language to limit escrow to genuine billing disputes > $25k and to define milestones for release (30/60 days). This avoids indefinite holds that impact capacity planning.

- Invoicing entity & tax routing: Your procurement packet suggests invoices to BlueHaven EU entity, but usage will be billed by Redwood US entity for the hosted product. For EU reverse-charge VAT treatment we require the tax evidence packet (attached Tax_Evidence_Routing.pdf). If BlueHaven insists on EU invoicing, we need a PO and local tax ID — otherwise Redwood must include VAT where applicable.

Quick asks from our side:
1) Can Procurement confirm whether Net 45 is a mandatory policy from your procurement team or negotiable at deal level?
2) Who will be the invoicing entity (BlueHaven, Inc. US vs BlueHaven Health GmbH)? Please include the VAT / tax ID if EU.
3) If you want escrow language tightened, we can provide the legal snippet below — would legal accept a tiered release schedule?

I’ve cc’d Ben (commercials) and Jonas (legal ops) to help with impact and language. If helpful, happy to jump on a quick 20-minute call to triage so we don’t block execution.

Thanks,

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form — escrow sequencing, invoicing entity & tax routing clarifications

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear redline. A few rapid answers and questions from our side: 

1) Net terms: Procurement policy prefers Net 45 for standard SaaS vendors; however, we can escalate to procurement leadership for key vendors. For the pilot scope (first 6 months / $150k), we do have flexibility to accept Net 60 pending Finance approval. For the expansion tranches we expect to revert to Net 45.

2) Invoicing entity: BlueHaven would like invoices to go to BlueHaven, Inc. (US) for now — we will provide a PO and the remittance address. For the EU teams (subscriptions used by EU ops), we will request a reversed-charge mechanism and will provide VAT IDs where applicable.

3) Escrow: Legal flagged the proposed release schedule — they want escrow held until formal dispute resolution or 90 days, whichever is earlier. We can accept a tiered release (30% at 30 days, remaining at resolution) if Redwood agrees to a cap on retained funds for operational continuity.

Attaching our internal redline (procurement_redline_BH_v2.docx) with track changes and a short procurement checklist.

Next steps: can Redwood confirm the pricing delta impact if we accept Net 60 for pilot only, then Net 45 for renewal? Also please confirm what tax evidence you need from our EU entity to apply reverse-charge.

Best,

Jane Cooper

Kimberly / Jonas — quick commercial read:

- Net terms effect: Moving from Net 60 to Net 45 decreases our DSO but materially the only material pricing lever is either a 0.5–1.0% financing uplift or a 30–60 day payment guarantee (letter of credit). For this deal size and runway (pilot $150k, expected ramp to $750k over 12 months) I recommend we: accept Net 60 for pilot (no uplift), commit to review at expansion and tie Net 45 to signed renewal or increased commit. This keeps initial go-live simple and limits approval friction.

- Escrow cap: I support a cap on escrow retained funds (suggest $100k or 20% of committed ARR for the first 12 months). That prevents indefinite operational cashstrain.

- Invoicing entity / tax: If invoices go to BlueHaven US, we can proceed normally; for EU reverse-charge we need VAT IDs and a signed certificate of business use. Tax_Evidence_Routing.pdf lists the exact files. If BlueHaven wants EU invoicing from month 1, we should price in potential VAT exposure until evidence is supplied.

If Legal accepts our proposed escrow release schedule (tiered release + cap), I think Procurement's suggested pilot Net60 concession is workable.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with BlueHaven Finance to finalize.

--
Ben Carter
Director, Commercials & GTM

Thanks — this is helpful and actionable. Summary / next steps: 

1) Net terms: Redwood will agree to Net 60 for the pilot tranche (first 6 months / $150k) with a written note in the Order Form. Net 45 will be the default thereafter unless BlueHaven provides a formal procurement waiver. Ben will document the commercial uplift scenario if Finance requires a pricing adjustment for Net 45.

2) Escrow: Redwood proposes final language: escrow only for disputes > $25k; release schedule 30% at 30 days, 40% at 60 days, remaining 30% at resolution or 90 days (whichever is earlier). Cap retention to $100k or 20% of committed ARR (whichever lower) for first 12 months. If legal pushes for 90-day hold without tiered release, we’ll need to evaluate operational liquidity — please let us know.

3) Tax / invoicing entity: BlueHaven to provide PO and remittance details for BlueHaven, Inc. (US) for month 1 invoices. For reverse-charge VAT on EU usage, please provide VAT IDs and completed tax evidence per the attached PDF. Jonas will prepare the final Order Form language reflecting the acceptance conditions for reverse charge.

4) Timeline: Redwood can provide an updated redline (v4) with the agreed bullets above by end of day Friday, Jun 13. Can BlueHaven confirm procurement/finance approval loop by Monday, Jun 16 so we can finalize signature before the planned pilot start (Jun 24)?

If that timeline works, I’ll route the v4 redline to Legal and Revenue Ops for sign-off and share a DocuSign link.

Thanks again — cc’ing Ben and Jonas for visibility.

Best,
